ns2:section.sectionText: This course examines the ways in which social factors (social norms, mobility, trust in medicine, health differentials, and socio-economic inequality) drive the spread of infectious pandemics across regions and develop differential patterns of infection (morbidity) and mortality across social groups. Students will examine how sociological views of disease, culture, health, inequality, and population inform the global social impacts of the COVID 19 pandemic. Learning Outcomes: Students will master the core elements of the fundamental cause of disease approach, gain insight into how social factors have contributed to previous pandemics, and critically access how the Fundamental Cause approach informs the development, and possible end, of the COVID-19 pandemic.
